intro: Dorian Pâquet plays Chopin’s Prelude in E minor, Op. 28 No. 4, marked Largo, on a Chavanne piano made in 2006.

sections.label: A · Melody over repeated left-hand quaver chords
sections.mNote: The left-hand chords change one note at a time.

sections.label: A′ · B returns above the chords
sections.mNote: The second phrase rises higher, then descends

sections.label: Coda · The last three chords
sections.mNote: A fermata over a rest precedes the cadence.

cues.title: Opening bars, left-hand chords
cues.text: The piano begins softly, espressivo. The first chord has G in the bass, with B and E above. The left hand repeats its chords while the notes within them gradually descend, and above them the melody holds B for three beats before moving to C.
cues.evidence: Peters edition, edited by Herrmann Scholtz (1900), bars 1–4. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=921
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

cues.title: Chavanne piano, 2006
cues.text: Pâquet plays a piano made by Chavanne. Vincent Chavanne began by making copies of old harpsichords in Toulouse, then turned to pianos and established his company in 1990. The piano on this recording dates from 2006.
cues.evidence: Instrument and recording date: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Prelude_op28_n4.wav. Company history: https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chavanne_(pianos)

cues.title: Stretto and forte, bars 16–19
cues.text: At bar 16 Chopin marks stretto. The right hand rises above its earlier narrow range, and the left hand reaches down to a low bass before the forte chords at bar 17. Chopin then writes diminuendo, then piano.
cues.evidence: Peters–Scholtz edition, bars 16–19: stretto, forte at bar 17, diminuendo and piano. https://www.mutopiaproject.org/cgibin/piece-info.cgi?id=921
cues.how: Timed from the score, aligned to this recording automatically.

transitions.title: B returns over E minor
transitions.from: A · Melody over repeated left-hand quaver chords
transitions.to: A′ · B returns above the chords
transitions.how: The left hand rests while the right hand plays a short flourish. B returns above an E minor chord with G in the bass, and the repeated quavers resume. The melody starts again from B, and at the written stretto it rises.

transitions.title: Fermata before the final chords
transitions.from: A′ · B returns above the chords
transitions.how: Under smorzando the accompaniment fades out. Its repeated quavers turn into a held chord, followed by a silence lengthened by a fermata. The last three chords are marked pianissimo. B7 resolves to E minor, and the melody rises a semitone from D♯ to E.

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: Composer for the piano, known for music that drew on operatic singing and on the irregular accents of the mazurka.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832 Chopin, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist, played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. He had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers, and teaching soon supplied his living. For the rest of his life his profession depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from one concert city to the next; Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. The family moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
